question: Did we create antibiotic resistance?
answer: We selected it; we did not invent it. Genes conferring resistance to several antibiotic classes have been recovered from 30,000-year-old permafrost, long before any human made a drug. Resistance is an ancient feature of microbial life that our use of antibiotics turned into an emergency.
move: Resistance genes are older than agriculture.
reference: D'Costa et al., Antibiotic resistance is ancient, Nature, 2011
